learning: Mass trend (0.6, 0.8, 1.0 kg: 55.4, 69.2, 73.3) shows diminishing returns. If 1.2 kg beats 73.33, the optimum is above 1.0 kg; if it falls back, 1.0 kg is near the local optimum. Next untested levers are wheel_radius and sensor_size; kd retuning for the heavier robot is still open.
notes: Complete robot for the 1.2 kg mass test on the iteration 7 baseline. Controller unchanged so that the mass effect is isolated and comparable with 73.33.
rationale: The Builder's proposal is a single-variable mass test on the best design so far (iteration 7, 1.0 kg, score 73.33). Mass has risen monotonically: 0.6 kg gave 55.45 (iteration 6), 0.8 kg gave 69.18 (iteration 3) and 1.0 kg gave 73.33 (iteration 7). The gain per 0.2 kg is shrinking (+14, then +4), so 1.2 kg is a fair test of whether the optimum lies above 1.0 kg. Geometry follows the proposal exactly: 80 mm sensor row (the contract maximum, which was monotone best), 12 mm sensors on a 12 mm pitch, 0.12 m track (0.10 and 0.14 m both scored worse), 0.03 m wheels, 0.12 m body width, 0.18 m body length, and mass 1.2 kg. Controller: I keep the iteration 7 gains (kp 0.8, kd 0.15, ki 0, base_speed 1.5, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]). The heavier robot has about 20 percent more yaw inertia than at 1.0 kg, so kd could need to rise, but no race has tested that. Changing kd now would confound the mass test, so I hold it fixed and let the next race show whether the s-bend and slalom oscillation (0.177 and 0.168 at 1.0 kg) rise. Max error has stayed at 0.060 to 0.067 m in every run, so the limit is still breached by bend transients rather than a steady offset.
